decisions.adopted_choice: F-sharp in m2, m6, m7 and m10, G-sharp in m8; remove E/G dyads wrongly inferred from the signs. In m7 the later F remains sharp by within-measure scope.

Compare clearer C-sharps in row 3 (20) and the F-sharps in row 4 (21,23). At m6 a staff line hides part of a cross-stroke, so a natural was explicitly considered. These are accidental signs, not independently stemmed E/G heads. Musical context: chromatic approaches F-sharp/G and G-sharp/A support this reading; harmony alone was not used to create sharps.
decisions.uncertainty: Low to moderate at m2,7,8,10; moderate at m6.

alternatives: C-natural in m3 remains the strongest symbol-confusion alternative.
decisions.location: page 1 row 1 m3; parallel row 2 m11
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: inspections 5 and 29 show the two uprights and both rising cross-strokes of m3's sign. Compare m11 in 12 and C-sharps in 20. The B naturals in 9/20 instead have offset rectangular crosspieces. Musical context: the written A7 and parallel phrase favor C-sharp, but are not the sole grounds.
decisions.uncertainty: Moderate at m3, where staff lines intersect the sign; low at m11.

decisions.adopted_choice: Eighth rest, F-sharp eighth, G quarter, G quarter.
alternatives: Candidate rest, F, A, A.
F-natural rather than F-sharp; see accidental decision.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: inspection 31 puts both final heads on the G line rather than the A space; compare the neighboring G notes of m7 in 6. The initial hook is an eighth rest. Musical context: the C7 label and repeated G support this, but do not determine staff placement.
decisions.uncertainty: Moderate because the noteheads trail below their main bodies.

decisions.adopted_choice: Remove the candidate's unison sustained overlays in these bars. Retain the visible moving line. Do not assign pitches to the long unheaded vertical strokes.
alternatives: Candidate sustained unisons at each long stroke.
An A4 half note under the final G/F pair of m3; its open-looking head is not secure enough to distinguish from the writer's partially hollow quarter heads.
Some long strokes may encode a performance convention not identifiable from this page.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: close-ups 12,14,26,29-32,39 show the moving heads with their own stems but no separate hollow sustained heads at the candidate's asserted pitches. Inspection 27 supplies a useful parallel: a long crossing vertical stroke stands between the second and third notes with no head, and the candidate had not treated that one as a voice. Small white centers occur even in visibly beamed eighth-note heads (25,35,39), so whiteness alone is not proof of a half note. The independently recognizable low C head in m44 is different and is retained. Musical context was not used to suppress or invent voices.
decisions.uncertainty: Moderate overall, higher in m3 and dense scale beams. Removed notes were not independently recoverable; this is not a reduction of securely visible polyphony.

decisions.adopted_choice: G-sharp eighth followed by A4 dotted half, seven eighths total; retain as an evidenced source-meter exception rather than add or shorten notes.
alternatives: Unmeasured G-sharp grace note into A dotted half.
A quarter/dotted-quarter with an omitted rest.
An overlapping second voice, whose head and alignment are not securely recoverable.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: surrounding row in 7 and close-ups 8/37 show the flagged initial note, large hollow following head and nearby dot. The long intervening vertical stroke has no secure separate pitched head. Musical context: chromatic G-sharp to A agrees with the F label, but cannot settle whether the first note was meant as a grace note.
decisions.uncertainty: High for duration/dot placement; moderate for pitches.

decisions.adopted_choice: Retain the candidate's moving-note reading in m9-14, apart from the corrected sharps and removal of unsupported overlays; m15 begins with C4 quarter, not a quarter rest.
alternatives: Candidate opening quarter rest in m15.
A lower note or rest if the separated stem/head are unrelated.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: row 2 view 7; m10-11 close-up 12; m14-15 views 17-19. The m15 opening has a low black head and a vertical stem like the low C gestures in m44, rather than a rest. D5 A4 F4 E4 in m13 is retained and rechecked in inspection 44; G B-flat A G in m9 is rechecked in 45. Ditto harmonies reproduce F, A7, Dm and E7 only where marked. Musical context: the low-register transition is plausible but not decisive; the surprising C against E7 is not harmonically corrected.
decisions.uncertainty: Moderate for m15 low C; low to moderate for the remaining moving line; p-like marking at m14 remains uncertain.

decisions.adopted_choice: A3 quarter then B-flat3 half, piano; replace the candidate's quarter rest plus E4 half.

A3 quarter then A3 half if the second oval lies on the ledger line.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: inspections 16 and 34 show two ledger levels beside the first black head, placing it at A3; the neighboring larger hollow head lies in the B3 space, with faint/interrupted continuity to the upward stem. A separate lower p-like flourish remains. Musical context: a low-register gesture between the E7 and D7 areas is possible, but does not prove these pitches. The B-flat is inherited from the active key signature, not an added accidental.

decisions.adopted_choice: Retain m17-19 and m21-22 moving notes, local accidentals and fermatas. Correct m20 middle note E5 to D5: B-natural eighth, D quarter, C-sharp dotted quarter with fermata.

G5 rather than A5 in m21, less consistent with its vertical placement.
Last m21 fermata applies to the pair as a whole.

The B natural signs are rectangular/cornered, unlike the rising double cross-strokes before C-sharp. m21 high A has a ledger indication and a fermata; the final f/e pair is retained with the fermata attached to f. decisions.uncertainty: Low to moderate for m20 D; moderate for the high A ledger; low for B-natural/C-sharp scope.

decisions.adopted_choice: Retain C-natural and explicit B-flat in m23; retain the two F-sharps in m25 and m27 and the moving notes of all six bars. Add a short slur over F-G in m27, not a tie.
alternatives: m27 curve is merely pen continuation; omit the slur.
m23 flat applies to C-flat rather than B-flat if the elongated head is read higher. Candidate B-flat retained as best staff-position reading.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: full row 21, m23 close-up 22 and m27 close-up 23. The signs before F have two crossed uprights; the C cancellation and following flat differ clearly in shape. The short low curved stroke in m27 links different pitches, so it cannot be a pitch tie. Musical context: the repeated m24/26 and m25/27 figures support the adopted notes; no extra accompaniment or chord was added in unmarked positions.
decisions.uncertainty: Moderate for exact endpoint of the m27 curve and m23's elongated B-flat head; low for F-sharp versus natural in the repeated figures.

decisions.adopted_choice: Retain all moving pitches and rhythms, the first/second ending signs, literal chord labels and marked harmony dittos. No new F-sharp is added to m40 despite the D7 label. Remove the spurious lower rest at m30 with its unsupported overlay.
alternatives: Treat a low mark at m30 as a subsidiary rest, as the candidate did.
Infer F-sharp from D7, rejected because not written.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: views 13,14,15,26,27,39 cover the complete scale figures and high-register D7 bar. The m30 mark beside the repeat is part of the flourish/dot region, not a securely independent quarter rest. The m40 first note is F without a written accidental; the chord does not authorize changing it. Musical context was used only to compare parallel m30/38 and m31/39, which agree.
decisions.uncertainty: Low to moderate for the moving notes; moderate for high-note ledger placement in m40.

decisions.adopted_choice: A5 eighth, A5 half, eighth rest. Replace the candidate's A eighth plus dotted half and p dynamic.
alternatives: Candidate A eighth plus A dotted half with a piano mark, an irregular seven-eighth bar.
A eighth, A dotted quarter, quarter rest.
Both A heads are parts of an overlapping-voice gesture.

The latter is adopted as an eighth rest; it is not securely connected as an augmentation dot to the half note. Small dots farther right may be ink/spatter. Musical context: a short breathing rest before the final phrase supports but does not prove the rest reading. The six-eighth count is a check, not the visual basis.
decisions.uncertainty: High; explicitly an editorial reconstruction, not a certain rest identification.

decisions.adopted_choice: Retain the moving line and F-sharp in m43. Preserve the separate low C4 half note in m44, entering after the first quarter as an editorial synchronization. Other candidate sustained unisons are removed. Retain the candidate p at m44 provisionally.
alternatives: Held C begins an eighth later and extends into the next bar.
The open C belongs to the beamed moving voice, not a separate held voice.
p-like glyph is a rest; not adopted in this bar because the moving rhythm is already complete.
decisions.reason: Visible evidence: row 24, close-up 25 and especially 33 show the distinct low hollow C head and ledger line in m44, unlike the unheaded crossing strokes elsewhere. The C half-note's exact horizontal onset is obscured by stems/beam; x2 synchronizes without adding an audible rest. Musical context: the written C7 supports C as a held pitch but is not its sole evidence. No ties are securely visible in these bars.
decisions.uncertainty: Moderate for the held C pitch, high for its onset; moderate for p versus a non-dynamic stroke.

resolution.adopted_choice: Retain ^G A6: a full-sized G-sharp eighth followed by A4 dotted half, totaling seven eighths under the prevailing written 3/4.
resolution.location: page 1, row 2 first bar; ABC source measure 8, part B
resolution.reason: Inspection 37, with surrounding row in inspection 7 and earlier close-up 8, shows the flagged first note and large hollow following head with a nearby dot. The adopted dotted-half reading is overfull in the source; shortening it or adding/removing rests would not be supported. The accidental is independently compared with the writer's other sharps. This is a declared source-reading exception, not a meter correction inferred from the validator.
resolution.uncertainty: High: the dot is displaced, and the first note could have been intended as an unmeasured grace note. A damaged overlapping voice is another possibility, but its alignment and independent head cannot be securely recovered.
